column1: # AQL Language Specification: Scalar/Micron — structured scalars
# Scalar/Micron is the structured-scalar family: values that behave as
# scalars (content equality, immutable, orderable) yet are object-like,
# exposing named read-only properties. Pathon (formerly Scalar/Path),
# Emailon, and Urlon are the builtin leaves; user Microns mint via
# `def Baron refine Micron {fields}`. Every type under Micron must have
# a name ending in the suffix "on" (one-directional rule — existing -on
# names elsewhere in the lattice are untouched).
# §0  Hard rename guard — the bare `Path` name is GONE. `Scalar/Path`
#     was moved into the family as `Scalar/Micron/Pathon` (keeping
#     FixedID 47; wire-identical). The old name must not resolve.
# §1  Construction — Emailon. String form (a plain user@host address)
#     and map form ({user host}) build the SAME value: the map form
#     re-renders through the string validator, so there is exactly one
# paired negatives — each malformed shape has its own error

column2: ERROR:Emailon source must be a string or map
ERROR:field host must be a String

column1: # §2  Construction — Urlon. Absolute URLs only (scheme://host…); the
#     map form re-renders to an href and re-parses it.

column2: ERROR:Urlon source must be a string or map

column1: # §3  Construction — the abstract root and Pathon under make.

column2: ERROR:Pathon source must be a list or string

column1: # §4  Properties — read-only, via dot/get (miss reads none) and the
#     strict twins dotr/getr (miss errors). Derived properties
#     (address / href / parts / abs) are synthesized at read time.
# get evaluates its key; dot quotes it

column3: forgiving read — unknown property is none

column1: # strict twins: a miss is a loud error
# has answers presence, including derived and optional fields
def e (make Emailon 'a@b.c') e has user/q
def e (make Emailon 'a@b.c') e has address/q
def e (make Emailon 'a@b.c') e has bogus/q
def u (make Urlon 'https://x.com/a') u has port/q
def u (make Urlon 'http://h.co:8080/p') u has port/q
# §5  Immutability — set on any Micron is an explicit error, on every
def e (make Emailon 'a@b.c') set user/q 'x' e
def u (make Urlon 'https://x.com/a') set host/q 'y' u
def p (make Pathon 'a/b') set abs/q true p
def Baron refine Micron {foo:String} end def b (make Baron {foo:'x'}) set foo/q 'y' b
# §6  Equality — content, not identity. Two Microns with the same
#     primary fields ARE equal; derived fields don't participate.
(make Urlon 'https://x.com/a?q=1') eq (make Urlon {scheme:'https' host:'x.com' path:'/a' query:'q=1'})
def Baron refine Micron {foo:String} end (make Baron {foo:'hi'}) eq (make Baron {foo:'hi'})
def Baron refine Micron {foo:String} end (make Baron {foo:'hi'}) eq (make Baron {foo:'ho'})
# newtype-vs-base: equal content compares TRUE across the nominal tag
def Workon refine Emailon end (make Workon 'a@b.c') eq (make Emailon 'a@b.c')
# §7  Ordering — Pathon keeps its historical order (segment count, then
#     reverse-lex segments, then relative-before-absolute); other leaves
#     order by canonical render; cross-kind pairs are cmp-incomparable
#     but tcmp-ordered by Rank (Micron < Pathon < Emailon < Urlon).

column3: shorter path first — verbatim old order

#     any Micron kind. Every bound name must end in "on" (case-

# §10  Open-words interplay. The builtin Micron leaves are BUILTINS —
#      a module cannot anchor a core-word extension on [Emailon
#      Emailon] (the module-scope rule requires an OriginUserDef type);
#      a user Micron minted inside the module DOES qualify.
import module [def add fn [[a:Emailon b:Emailon] [Boolean] [true]] export "M" {add: add/r}]
column3: builtin Micron leaves do not anchor module extensions
